### Tools

| Tool | What it does | Read-only | Destructive | Posture |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `list_messages` | List the signed-in user's messages across folders, newest first, or search them. search is a keyword query whose value includes its double quotes, for example "pizza" or "from:alice@example.com" with the quotes; filter takes OData, for example isRead eq false. Keep results small with select (for example subject,from,receivedDateTime,bodyPreview) and top (1-1000, default 10); the response's @odata.nextLink holds the next page. | yes | no | auto |
| `list_folder_messages` | List the messages of one mail folder, newest first. mailFolder-id is a folder id from list\_mail\_folders or a well-known name: inbox, drafts, sentitems, deleteditems, archive or junkemail. filter, orderby, select and top (1-1000, default 10) work as in list\_messages; @odata.nextLink holds the next page. | yes | no | auto |
| `get_message` | Read one message by its id (from list\_messages), with its body, sender, recipients and conversationId. | yes | no | auto |
| `list_mail_folders` | List the mailbox's top-level folders, such as Inbox, Drafts and Sent Items, with their ids and unread counts. | yes | no | auto |
| `create_draft` | Save a new message in Drafts without sending it; send\_draft sends it later by its id. The input body is the message, for example {"subject": "Q3 numbers", "body": {"contentType": "text", "content": "Hi Bob, ..."}, "toRecipients": \[{"emailAddress": {"address": "bob@example.com"}}\]}. | no | no | ask |
| `create_reply_draft` | Create a reply draft to a message, by its id, in the same conversation, without sending it. Comment is the reply text, for example "Thanks, Thursday at 3pm works.". Returns the draft, whose id send\_draft takes. | no | no | ask |
| `send_draft` | Send a draft, by its id (from create\_draft or create\_reply\_draft). A copy is saved in Sent Items. | no | no | ask |
| `send_mail` | Send a new message in one call; a copy is saved in Sent Items. The input body is {"Message": {...}}, for example {"Message": {"subject": "Lunch", "body": {"contentType": "text", "content": "Friday at 1?"}, "toRecipients": \[{"emailAddress": {"address": "bob@example.com"}}\]}}. | no | no | ask |
| `reply_to_message` | Reply to the sender of a message, by its id, in the same conversation, and send it. Comment is the reply text, for example "Thanks, Thursday at 3pm works.". | no | no | ask |
| `reply_all` | Reply to the sender and every recipient of a message, by its id, in the same conversation, and send it. Comment is the reply text. | no | no | ask |
| `update_message` | Change a message's read state, categories, flag or importance, by its id, for example {"isRead": true} or {"flag": {"flagStatus": "flagged"}}. | no | no | ask |
| `move_message` | Move a message, by its id, to another folder: DestinationId is a folder id or a well-known name such as archive or deleteditems. A move to deleteditems deletes the message, so this tool is destructive. | no | yes | deny |
| `list_calendars` | List the user's calendars, with their ids, names, owners and whether the user can edit each one. | yes | no | auto |
| `list_calendar_view` | List the events of the user's default calendar between startDateTime and endDateTime, with recurring occurrences expanded, for example startDateTime=2026-10-21T00:00:00Z and endDateTime=2026-10-28T00:00:00Z. select (for example subject,start,end,location,attendees,organizer) keeps results small; top is 1-1000; @odata.nextLink holds the next page. | yes | no | auto |
| `get_event` | Read one event by its id (from list\_calendar\_view), with its time, location, organizer, attendees and their responses, and its online meeting link. | yes | no | auto |
| `get_schedule` | Return the free/busy availability of people or rooms between StartTime and EndTime, each {"dateTime": "2026-10-22T09:00:00", "timeZone": "Pacific Standard Time"}, for example Schedules=\["bob@example.com"\]. AvailabilityViewInterval is the slot length in minutes (default 30). | yes | no | auto |
| `create_event` | Create an event in the user's default calendar. The input body is the event, for example {"subject": "Design review", "start": {"dateTime": "2026-10-22T15:00:00", "timeZone": "Pacific Standard Time"}, "end": {...}, "location": {"displayName": "Room 4"}, "attendees": \[{"emailAddress": {"address": "bob@example.com"}, "type": "required"}\]}. Each attendee gets an invitation; isOnlineMeeting true adds an online meeting. | no | no | ask |
| `update_event` | Change an event, by its id: the input body holds only the fields to change, for example {"start": {"dateTime": "2026-10-22T16:00:00", "timeZone": "Pacific Standard Time"}, "end": {...}} to move it. If the user organizes it and it has attendees, they get the update. | no | no | ask |
| `accept_event` | Accept a meeting invitation, by the event's id. Comment is an optional note to the organizer; SendResponse false accepts without telling the organizer (default true). | no | no | ask |
| `tentatively_accept_event` | Tentatively accept a meeting invitation, by the event's id. Comment is an optional note to the organizer; SendResponse false responds without telling the organizer (default true). | no | no | ask |
| `decline_event` | Decline a meeting invitation, by the event's id. Comment is an optional note to the organizer; SendResponse false declines without telling the organizer (default true). | no | no | ask |
| `delete_event` | Delete an event by its id. If the user organizes it, the attendees get a cancellation. | no | yes | deny |

| `fetch` | Generic tool: per-tool policy sees only the verb; the operation is in `entityUrls`. Read one or more Microsoft 365 entities by Graph resource path, such as /me/messages or /me/events/{event-id}. | yes | no | ask |
| `fetch_blob` | Generic tool: per-tool policy sees only the verb; the operation is in `path`. Read binary content by Graph resource path, such as a OneDrive file's content, returned as Base64. | yes | no | ask |
| `call_function` | Generic tool: per-tool policy sees only the verb; the operation is in `functionUrl`. Call a Microsoft Graph function by resource path, such as /me/calendarview with a time window. | yes | no | ask |
| `create_entity` | Generic tool: per-tool policy sees only the verb; the operation is in `parentUrl`, `jsonBody`. Create a Microsoft 365 entity in a collection, such as an event in /me/events. Blocked by tenant policy until an admin allows writes. | no | no | deny |
| `update_entity` | Generic tool: per-tool policy sees only the verb; the operation is in `entityUrl`, `jsonBody`. Change the fields of a Microsoft 365 entity by resource path. Blocked by tenant policy until an admin allows writes. | no | yes | deny |
| `delete_entity` | Generic tool: per-tool policy sees only the verb; the operation is in `entityUrl`. Delete a Microsoft 365 entity by resource path. Blocked by tenant policy until an admin allows writes. | no | yes | deny |
| `do_action` | Generic tool: per-tool policy sees only the verb; the operation is in `actionUrl`, `jsonBody`. Run a Microsoft Graph action by resource path, such as /me/messages/{message-id}/send. Blocked by tenant policy until an admin allows writes. | no | yes | deny |
| `ask` | Generic tool: per-tool policy sees only the verb; the operation is in `question`, `agentId`. Ask Microsoft 365 Copilot, or another agent by id, a question in natural language; billed in Copilot Credits. | no | no | deny |
| `list_agents` | List the Microsoft 365 Copilot agents the user can ask, with their ids and publishers. | yes | no | auto |
| `get_schema` | Return the JSON Schema or TypeScript definition of a Graph path or operation, for fetch, create or update. | yes | no | auto |
| `search_paths` | Find the Graph resource paths that match a prefix or a regular expression, such as messages. | yes | no | auto |
